name: Caen Carpiquet airport
before:
The airport for Caen, at Carpiquet 6 km west of the city in Calvados, Normandy.

It is small and growing fast. Passenger numbers went from 180,910 in 2017 to 274,011 in 2018. Chalair Aviation has its head office here.

There is one concrete runway of 1,900 metres with high intensity approach lighting, plus two grass strips used by light aircraft. Runway 31 carries a Category III instrument landing system, which is generous for an airport this size. Twisto bus line 3 has served the airport since June 2015.

The site has its own place in the 1944 story. It opened as Air Base 720 in August 1939, was taken by the Luftwaffe in June 1940 and used as a rear base during the Battle of Britain, and was fought over at length by Anglo-Canadian and German troops during the Battle of Normandy.
after:
The airport for Caen, at Carpiquet 6 km west of the city in Normandy.

It is small, with just over 300,000 passengers in 2025. Chalair Aviation has its head office here.

The main runway is 1,900 metres long, and there is also a grass strip. Twisto bus line 3 has served the airport since June 2015.

The site has its own place in the 1944 story. It opened as an air base in August 1939, was taken over by the Germans in June 1940 and was fought over by Canadian and German troops in July 1944, during the Battle of Normandy.

sources.quote: is an international airport located in Carpiquet, 6 km west of Caen

claims.note: The French AIP (valid from 6 August 2026) gives 6 km west. The coordinates give 7.0 km in a straight line at 262 degrees, which is west. The operator's pilot sheet says 8 km west, probably by road, and its About page says 10 minutes from the centre; the official 6 km is kept because it passes the coordinates check.

claims.inAfter: It is small, with just over 300,000 passengers in 2025.
claims.note: Was 180,910 in 2017 and 274,011 in 2018. UAF (figures supplied by the operators) gives 307,860 for 2025 and Eurostat 305,767, 0.7 per cent apart, so the text rounds to 'just over 300,000'. Caen ranks 23rd of the French airports in the UAF table, which carries 'small'.

claims.claim: opened as an air base in August 1939
claims.inAfter: It opened as an air base in August 1939
claims.note: Was 'Air Base 720'. Wikipedia numbers it 720 and the commune of Carpiquet 131; both give the opening as 17 August 1939, so the date stays and the number goes.

la base aérienne de Caen-Carpiquet n°131, officiellement inauguré le 17 août 1939

claims.claim: taken over by the Germans in June 1940
claims.inAfter: was taken over by the Germans in June 1940
claims.note: Was 'taken by the Luftwaffe'. The commune says the Germans took over the base in June 1940; 'Luftwaffe' is Wikipedia's word alone.

sources.quote: Captured by the Luftwaffe in June 1940
En juin 1940, les Allemands héritent d'une base aérienne moderne et pratiquement terminée.

claims.claim: fought over by Canadian and German troops in July 1944, Battle of Normandy
claims.inAfter: was fought over by Canadian and German troops in July 1944, during the Battle of Normandy
claims.note: Was 'fought over at length by Anglo-Canadian and German troops'. The commune describes the Canadian attack on 4 July 1944 (Operation Windsor) and says the airfield stayed in German hands until 9 July; 'Anglo' and 'at length' rest on Wikipedia alone.

sources.quote: In June and July 1944, during the Battle of Normandy, Anglo-Canadian and German troops engaged in long and harsh fights over control of the strategically important aerodrome.

quote: Les troupes canadiennes (8e brigade et The Royal Winnipeg Rifles), commandées par le général Dempsey, lancent une offensive (l'opération Windsor) sur Carpiquet le 4 juillet 1944 afin de libérer l'aéroport qui était un objectif prioritaire du débarquement de Normandie.
reste aux mains des forces allemandes jusqu'au 9 juillet

claims.why: Only Wikipedia says so plainly. Normandy is kept, in the operator's own words.

claims.wasBefore: It is small and growing fast.
claims.why: No longer true. UAF: 307,860 in 2025, 1.0 per cent above 2019 (304,769); Eurostat: 301,285 in 2022 and 305,767 in 2025. 'Small' is kept with the 2025 figure.

claims.wasBefore: Passenger numbers went from 180,910 in 2017 to 274,011 in 2018.
claims.why: Seven and eight years stale; replaced by the 2025 figure from UAF and Eurostat.

claims.wasBefore: There is one concrete runway of 1,900 metres
claims.why: The surface is asphalt (operator: tarmac; AIP: bituminous concrete; OurAirports: ASP), so 'concrete' misleads, and the surface is no use to an agent. The length is kept.
True (AIP and operator) but of no use to a travel agent; dropped with the landing-system sentence.

claims.claim: two grass strips used by light aircraft
claims.wasBefore: plus two grass strips used by light aircraft
claims.why: The AIP, the operator and OurAirports list one grass strip, not two; corrected to one. Who uses it is not stated by a second source.

claims.claim: Runway 31 Category III ILS, generous for its size
claims.wasBefore: Runway 31 carries a Category III instrument landing system, which is generous for an airport this size.
claims.why: Wrong. The runway is now numbered 12/30, and both the French AIP (valid 6 August 2026: 'RWY 30 equipped with an ILS CAT 1 only') and the operator's technical sheet ('ILS : cat. I') give Category I. Once corrected there is nothing notable left to say, so the sentence goes.

claims.wasBefore: It opened as Air Base 720 in August 1939
claims.why: The base number is disputed (Wikipedia 720, the commune 131). Softened to 'an air base', with the date both agree on.

claims.wasBefore: was taken by the Luftwaffe in June 1940
claims.why: Softened to 'taken over by the Germans', which both sources say.

claims.claim: rear base during the Battle of Britain
claims.wasBefore: used as a rear base during the Battle of Britain
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the commune's history does not mention it and no other source was reachable (the web archive is blocked here).

claims.claim: fought over at length by Anglo-Canadian troops
claims.wasBefore: was fought over at length by Anglo-Canadian and German troops
claims.why: Softened to Canadian and German troops in July 1944, which both sources say.

opinion.text: The site has its own place in the 1944 story.
opinion.why: The old text's lead-in to the history, kept; the July 1944 fighting it introduces is sourced in the next sentence.
